title: Flood Warning
description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties. .Heavy rainfall working through the basin will cause river levels on the St. Johns at Deland to continue rising through Major Flood Stage. The river is forecast to rise above its former record crest this weekend, reaching 6.4 feet, where it is expected to linger into early next week. For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. The river is forecast to rise above the flood of record. * WHERE...St Johns River near Deland. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 1:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 5.9 feet. - Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 1:30 PM EST Wednesday was 5.9 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 6.4 feet Saturday evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter. - Flood stage is 4.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

title: Flood Warning
description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County. .Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns Above Lake Harney near Geneva to remain within Major Flood Stage, above its previous record flood stage. River levels are forecast to hold near a crest of 13.2 to 13.3 feet through late week, before beginning a very slow decline within Major flood stage this weekend. For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. The river crest has surpassed its previous flood of record. * WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 10.8 feet, Water covers State Road 46 and it may become impassable near Jungle Road and Prevatt Road. Standing water on secondary roads near the river deepens to more than three feet in some areas. Flooding becomes more significant to structures and marinas from above Lake Harney to the Lake Jesup area. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 1:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 13.2 feet. - Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 1:30 PM EST Wednesday was 13.2 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 13.3 feet this evening. - Flood stage is 8.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

title: Flood Warning
description: ...The National Weather Service in Seattle has issued a Flood Warning for the following rivers in Washington... Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County. .Heavy rain over the Olypics overnight plus an additional 2-4 inches of rain, with snow levels well above mountain tops will drive the Skokomish River above flood stage this afternoon to above Moderate flood. * WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast. This approaches the flood of record. * WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch. * WHEN...From this afternoon to Friday evening. * IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 8:30 AM PST Wednesday the stage was 15.6 feet. - Forecast...The river will rise above flood stage this afternoon to 17.9 feet late tonight. It will then fall below flood stage late Friday morning. Further rises through the weekend are likely, with exceeding flood stage possible. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
